transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-12-18
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Recording: Fireflies auto-transcript (medium quality)
Attendees: Dana (Redwood AE), Evan (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood), Oliver (Larkspur CISO), Nina (Cloud Infra Lead), Samir (Security Architect), Jade (Compliance)

Summary: quick deep-dive of on-prem/VPC security posture, network zoning, inbound/outbound controls, firewall/NAT patterns, KMS/HSM integration options, audit log collection and SOC2 artifacts required for onboarding Redwood Private. Customer requests very tight egress policy and key custody assurances.

Topics discussed:
- Network zoning and segmentation (management vs workload plane)
- Ingress patterns: bastion/jump-host, LB, private control plane connectivity
- Egress controls: allowlists, egress proxies, model downloads, telemetry endpoints
- KMS integration: BYOK, HSM vs cloud KMS, key wrapping, key rotation and key availability SLA
- Audit logs and SIEM integration: Splunk, retention, signed logs for compliance
- RBAC/SSO: SAML, SCIM, service accounts, session recording for audit

Action item recap at end (see metadata)

Transcript body:
00:00:05 Dana (AE): Hey everyone thanks for making time. quick intro, I'm Dana from Redwood Inference, I'm the AE on this account. Evan's our SE and he'll run most of the tech part, Priya's taking notes. Oliver, Nina, Samir, Jade, thanks for joining. Can you give a quick recap of Larkspur's security posture and what you want to validate today?
00:00:28 Oliver (CISO): Yeah sure, hi all. We're Larkspur Financial, heavily regulated, EU data residency plus some APAC constraints. We're evaluating Redwood Private to run inference behind our network controls. Key asks are: complete network isolation for inference workloads, strict egress allowlist, customer-controlled KMS, and SOC2-ready audit trails. Also want to confirm we can run without any public ingress other than approved management channels.
00:00:50 Nina (Cloud Infra): to add, we do mix of on-prem baremetal and a private cloud region. We use an egress proxy and a forward proxy for TLS interception to monitor outbound. We also have a dedicated SIEM (Splunk) and require audit log forwarding.
00:01:05 Evan (SE): great, that's helpful. we'll walk through typical private deployment topology, where there are two planes -- control plane and data/worker plane. Important note: our private option gives you a customer-controlled control plane that talks to the management API over a private peering link or can be air-gapped if required.
00:01:22 Samir (Security Architect): couple quick clarifying q's: does Redwood require outbound 443 from workers for telemetry or model pulls? And do workers need to call back to a redwood-hosted auth endpoint?
00:01:39 Evan (SE): good q. by default our agents check for updates and for model artifact pulls they usually reach out to our artifact store, but for private/onprem we support two modes: 1) packaged model bundle pushed to the cluster (offline model load) or 2) workers allowed to pull from a customer-hosted artifact repo (your nexus or artifactory) where we only need internal access. Telemetry and phone-home can be disabled; we do recommend at least a controlled channel for health telemetry, but it's optional and can go through your egress proxy. so no mandatory internet egress to a public redwood endpoint for core inference.
00:02:12 Oliver (CISO): ok offline model load is preferred for high-security workloads. what's the install process for that? any signed artifacts?
00:02:21 Evan (SE): we provide signed model bundles — they are SHA256 signed and we provide a signing public key that you can verify. install is an offline bundle you apply to the cluster. For updates you can either accept a signed bundle via your internal artifactory or we can arrange secure file transfer.
00:02:35 Nina (Cloud Infra): about network zoning, we require separate VLANs/subnets for management and inference workers. Management subnet should be able to reach Redwood control plane over private peering, and workers should be in a more locked-down subnet with egress limited to the egress proxy. Is that standard?
00:02:51 Evan (SE): Yes, that's the recommended pattern. We typically recommend three zones: management/ops, inference workers, and a model artifact store. Management hosts run the operator and control-plane agents; they need outbound to the control plane (unless you choose air-gapped). Workers can be totally isolated except for talking to model store, egress proxy, and your KMS endpoints if using networked KMS.
00:03:10 Samir (Security Architect): let's dig into egress: can we force all outbound through a TLS-inspecting forward proxy? will the agents tolerate MITM proxying?
00:03:21 Evan (SE): agents support proxy config. if you do TLS inspection, you'll need to install your root CA into the runtime image or have the proxy do TLS passthrough for certain hostnames. we recommend TLS passthrough for KMS endpoints and signed bundle verification to avoid breaking signature checks. for general telemetry you can proxy it.
00:03:40 Jade (Compliance): from SOC2 perspective we need immutable audit logs and proof of key custody. How does Redwood log admin actions and where are those logs stored?
00:03:53 Evan (SE): audit events are emitted from the management plane; for Private, audit logs can be pushed to your SIEM (syslog/HTTP/forwarder). We can also write logs to a customer-owned S3 or NFS with write-once policies. Events include: model loads, config changes, user role changes, token issuance. We sign logs with an HMAC + timestamp to provide tamper evidence.
00:04:16 Oliver (CISO): do you provide log integrity proofs? chain of custody?
00:04:21 Evan (SE): yes we can provide signed log digests on a periodic cycle. For the highest assurance we support forwarding to your HSM-backed storage or a WORM bucket and also can optionally ship signed hashes to an external attestation service.
00:04:35 Nina (Cloud Infra): KMS: we want BYOK, keys in our HSM vendor (Thales/Luna), not cloud KMS. what are the options for integrating an on-prem HSM?
00:04:47 Evan (SE): we support three KMS patterns: 1) customer-managed cloud KMS (AWS/Azure/GCP) via network calls, 2) on-prem HSM accessed via a KMIP proxy or gateway, and 3) envelope encryption where the local runtime uses a locally held wrapping key and we manage ephemeral keys. For HSMs, we integrate with a KMIP gateway or a network bridge. Keys never leave your HSM — Redwood only receives wrapped keys or uses an HSM-backed signing flow.
00:05:12 Samir (Security Architect): latencies? if every inference needs to call KMS for unwrap, that's going to add latency.
00:05:19 Evan (SE): we use envelope encryption and cache unwrapped DEKs in memory (ephemeral) at worker process level — KV cache — with strict lifetime and secure memory wiping on rotation/evict. so per-token KMS calls are not required. unwrap on model load or key rotation; then runtime uses in-memory DEK. reduces latency.
00:05:37 Jade (Compliance): rotation cadence? evidence for rotation required by ISO and SOC frameworks.
00:05:44 Evan (SE): rotation is configurable. we record rotation events in the audit log and can snapshot key versions. We can automate rotation via your KMS or through an operator that triggers wrap/unwrap flows.
00:05:55 Oliver (CISO): firewalling specifics: ports to open? NAT?
00:05:59 Evan (SE): minimal set: management plane -> control plane: TCP 443 or privatelink/peering. management -> worker plane: API ports for orchestration (we'll provide the exact list). workers -> model store: TCP 443 or internal port for artifactory. egress proxy on port 3128 (or your standard). no inbound from public to worker subnets; inbound only via LB/bastion in management zone. We'll send a ports matrix in the follow-up.
00:06:30 Nina (Cloud Infra): Do you recommend a bastion host or an agent-based ephemeral session broker for admin access?
00:06:37 Evan (SE): bastion is simplest and compliant with many controls, but we support ephemeral session broker (SSO-integrated) that uses short-lived service tokens and records session activity to the audit log. That reduces attack surface and avoids opening broad SSH ports.
00:06:53 Samir (Security Architect): about model artifacts and checksum verification — you mentioned signed bundles. do you also support signed container images for the runtime?
00:07:02 Evan (SE): yes images can be signed (cosign) and you can run an admission controller to block unsigned images. We also support scanning on the image registry before deployment.
00:07:16 Dana (AE): quick interruption — curious about data residency: inference data, prompts, embeddings — do any of those leave the worker? we need to ensure no PII or card data is sent offsite.
00:07:29 Evan (SE): by default for Private the inference data stays in your network. telemetry can be disabled. If you configure a telemetry channel it can be routed through your proxy and scrubbed. embeddings and logs can be configured to persist only to customer-owned storage. We also support token redaction for certain fields at the agent level.
00:07:48 Nina (Cloud Infra): question on registry access: if we keep model store private behind authentication, can workers authenticate via short-lived certs instead of static passwords?
00:07:58 Evan (SE): yes we support mTLS and short-lived certs issued by your CA; the operator can provision certs to workers with limited TTL.
00:08:08 Jade (Compliance): SOC2 auditors will also look for identity provisioning and deprovisioning proof. how does Redwood integrate with SSO/SAML and SCIM?
00:08:19 Evan (SE): we support SAML SSO for user login, and SCIM for provisioning groups and users. Audit events include login events, role changes, and SSO session data. For compliance we can export SCIM logs and provisioning history.
00:08:34 Oliver (CISO): what about service accounts used by the runtime — how are their credentials rotated and audited?
00:08:41 Evan (SE): service accounts use short-lived tokens and are issued by the management plane with RBAC scoping. tokens rotate frequently and issuance is recorded in audit logs. For extra security we can integrate with your vault (HashiCorp Vault) so secrets never land in plaintext on disk.
00:08:58 Samir (Security Architect): edge case: if a worker gets compromised, can it exfiltrate model weights or user prompts? how do we mitigate that?
00:09:07 Evan (SE): multiple mitigations: 1) network microsegmentation so workers can't reach management or artifact stores except on specific ports; 2) disk encryption for model artifacts and process-level memory protections; 3) limit log detail for user prompts and apply redaction; 4) runtime enforces least privilege and we can enable seccomp/SELinux policies in the runtime container. Also recommended: runtime attestation and integrity checks on boot.
00:09:35 Nina (Cloud Infra): curious about OS patching and CVE management for the runtime nodes. do you provide a patch baseline or images?
00:09:43 Evan (SE): we provide hardened base images and a regular patch cadence. For Private, customers can bring their own images or use Redwood-provided images. We provide CVE reports and assist with triage. We can also integrate with your vulnerability management pipeline.
00:09:58 Dana (AE): moving into more specifics — Nina you mentioned egress proxy config; do you have a sample we can look at?
00:10:04 Nina (Cloud Infra): yes we'll share a proxy.conf and our allowlist rules. currently only a handful of external destinations allowed for management hosts, and nothing for worker plane except internal artifactory.
00:10:14 Evan (SE): perfect. we will prepare a mapping of which components need what destinations and sample proxy rules. we'll also call out TLS passthrough requirement for KMS HSM endpoints to avoid interception.
00:10:27 Samir (Security Architect): about attestation: can we require the worker to provide a TPM quote or some attestation back to control plane before accepting workloads?
00:10:36 Evan (SE): yes we support optional hardware attestation. You can configure the operator to verify node attestation (TPM or cloud provider instance identity) before scheduling workloads.
00:10:49 Jade (Compliance): retention windows — for audit logs we need 7 years retention for some EU regs. can you handle that?
00:10:57 Evan (SE): logs will be forwarded to your SIEM where retention is controlled by you; for any logs we retain in our control plane we'll adhere to agreed retention and can export on request. For long-term retention we recommend your S3/WORM solution.
00:11:09 Oliver (CISO): trickier: we want to run a canary with minimal data and then ramp; what are rollback procedures if we see a data leak?
00:11:18 Evan (SE): rollback: operator can revert to backup config and revoke tokens for the canary cluster; we also support immediate network isolation of a node pool. We can also rotate keys and re-wrap model artifacts. All those actions are audit-logged.
00:11:34 Dana (AE): switching to legal/compliance: Jade any questions about SOC2 evidence we should prepare?
00:11:40 Jade (Compliance): yes we'll need documented operational policies, evidence of access reviews, incident response runbooks, and encryption key management proofs. A SOC2-friendly onboarding packet with evidence templates would be ideal.
00:11:53 Dana (AE): we'll provide a SOC2 evidence starter pack and examples of artifacts we've supplied to other customers.
00:12:00 Priya (Redwood): note — action item: compile list of control mappings (how Redwood features map to SOC2/ISO controls).
00:12:07 Nina (Cloud Infra): another technical note: we use a private PKI, and for images we want the runtime to verify images with cosign and a cosign key in our key store. possible?
00:12:16 Evan (SE): absolutely. cosign verification can be enforced at admission time, and cosign keys can live in your Vault/HSM.
00:12:23 Samir (Security Architect): talk me through an example flow for KMS HSM unwrap with KMIP gateway.
00:12:30 Evan (SE): flow: operator requests wrapped key from your artifact store, then uses KMIP gateway to request unwrap using HSM. The unwrapped DEK is kept in process memory only and rotated. We log the unwrap event to SIEM with context, including which HSM slot/key id was used.
00:12:47 Oliver (CISO): are we able to run the control plane entirely on-prem so there's zero transit to redwood cloud?
00:12:55 Evan (SE): yes we offer fully private control plane deployment (on-prem) where the entire management API and console run inside your network; in that case the only Redwood contact is professional services for upgrades unless you open a maintenance channel. It increases operational responsibility on the customer but satisfies zero-transit requirements.
00:13:13 Nina (Cloud Infra): upgrades — how are they handled in air-gapped setups?
00:13:18 Evan (SE): we provide signed upgrade bundles that you can apply offline. PS can do the upgrade remotely if you allow a temporary secure channel or we ship offline media.
00:13:27 Samir (Security Architect): we need to validate the immutability of audit records. how do you prove logs haven't been tampered with?
00:13:34 Evan (SE): we provide HMAC-signed log blocks and we can ship periodic signed digests to an external attestation service or to a write-once storage. We can also integrate with blockchain-style append-only logs if you want tamper-evidence.
00:13:47 Jade (Compliance): excellent. another regulatory point: data deletion requests — if a user asks to delete prompts/embeddings, how do you ensure deletion across caching layers and backups?
00:13:58 Evan (SE): we have a deletion workflow that invalidates keys and purges cached DEKs and KV prefixes; we track deletions in audit logs. For backups we catalog snapshots and can issue a purge for the specific artifacts, but full deletion of immutable backups depends on retention policies; we'll work with your retention and legal teams.
00:14:20 Nina (Cloud Infra): want to confirm regarding network ACLs: can we block all egress from worker pool except to 10.1.5.10:443 (artifactory) and to 10.2.1.1:636 (LDAPS) and to our KMS gateway 10.3.4.2:5696?
00:14:35 Evan (SE): that's fine. we'll provide the exact port matrix; the only caveat is if you enable metrics shipping to our hosted console you'd need to open for those endpoints — but you can choose not to ship metrics.
00:14:47 Oliver (CISO): would you support a model where we use a separate air-gapped cluster for high-sensitivity customers and a less-restricted cluster for lower risk?
00:14:56 Evan (SE): yes cluster-per-class-of-data is recommended. Canary and non-prod can be in a less restricted environment and we can promote models across clusters using signed bundles.
00:15:09 Dana (AE): we'll summarize next steps and deliverables at the end. quick quick comments: any blockers for a pilot?
00:15:17 Nina (Cloud Infra): main blockers: need KMS/HSM integration pattern sign-off, confirm offline model load process with signed bundles, and verify audit log retention and forwarding meets our policy. Also need a clear ports list.
00:15:31 Dana (AE): great, Evan will take KMS and network deliverables, I'll follow up on SOC2 artifacts.
00:15:38 Priya (Redwood): note — scheduling workshop for model load and KMS integration (aiming week of 12/29).
00:15:47 Dana (AE): ok let's fast forward — technical deep dive transcripts (jumps)
00:16:12 Speaker 1 (customer): so if we use KMIP, do you support PKCS#11 or only KMIP?
00:16:20 Evan (SE): we have adapters. KMIP is common but we can work with PKCS#11 via a gateway or local agent that proxies calls.
00:16:33 Speaker 2 (customer): how do you handle secrets in logs? sometimes stack traces leak env vars
00:16:40 Evan (SE): we redacted env vars in logs by default and can add filtering rules, also log scrubbing at forwarder stage.
00:16:50 Speaker 3 (customer): if we want mutual TLS to the artifact store, how are client certs rotated?
00:16:55 Evan (SE): short-lived certs via your CA, operator auto-rotates. we keep rotation events in audit logs.
00:17:05 Speaker 1 (customer): OOF, can you run an offline benchmark? we need to measure end-to-end latency with KMS unwrap only at model load
00:17:12 Evan (SE): yes we can do a lab benchmark. we'll schedule a perf run with your cluster — will need representative payloads and model size.
00:17:22 Speaker 2 (customer): what about making sure the cluster doesn't reach out to public dockerhub for images?
00:17:28 Evan (SE): you'll run a private registry and we'll configure admission to block external registries.
00:17:33 Speaker 3 (customer): one more — how do we prove to auditors that Redwood didn't access customer data?
00:17:38 Dana (AE): proof: private control plane, audit logs showing no external connections, signed digests, and PS statement of data handling. we'll provide docs.
00:18:00 --- (mid-call break) ---
00:30:05 Evan (SE): continuing — specifics for firewall rules: we'll give a CSV of ip/port/service. example: 
- management -> control plane: 10.10.10.0/24:443 (or peering)
- management -> workers: 10.20.0.0/24:2379,8500 (or control ports)
- workers -> model store: 10.30.0.5:443 (mTLS)
- workers -> KMS gateway: 10.3.4.2:5696 (KMIP/TLS)
- workers -> egress proxy: 10.40.1.2:3128
No public 0.0.0.0/0 inbound to workers.
00:31:10 Nina (Cloud Infra): we will need to test with our forward proxy; we'll send sample proxy logs.
00:31:20 Evan (SE): also note DNS requirements — workers need to resolve internal names; if you're blocking external DNS we support static host entries or a local DNS forwarder.
00:31:32 Samir (Security Architect): how do you handle crash dumps in memory that may include prompts?
00:31:38 Evan (SE): core dumps are disabled by default; memory is zeroed on process exit. We also recommend restricting /proc access and enabling container hardening.
00:31:50 Jade (Compliance): for evidence we need: key lifecycle docs, log forwarding config, network diagram, and an attestation of signed-bundle verification.
00:32:00 Dana (AE): we'll assemble those artifacts.
00:32:05 Priya (Redwood): note action: create mapping doc for SOC2 controls -> Redwood features.
00:32:10 Oliver (CISO): final question on user access: do you support role separation (dev vs ops vs security) with time-limited elevated roles?
00:32:18 Evan (SE): yes RBAC supports granular roles and just-in-time elevation with approval flows. Those elevation events are audit-logged.
00:32:28 Nina (Cloud Infra): any concerns about storage encryption for model weights?
00:32:34 Evan (SE): at-rest encryption is mandatory and keys are customer-controlled when BYOK is enabled. disk encryption + object encryption for model stores.
00:32:45 Samir (Security Architect): we might want to run a purple-team exercise pre-pilot. Redwood ok with that?
00:32:51 Dana (AE): yes, we support red-team/purple-team tests in a sandbox window; we just ask for notice and a scoped engagement.
00:33:00 Evan (SE): quick note on observability — for latency-sensitive workloads we recommend local metrics collection and only push aggregates out; that way you keep low-level traces internal.
00:33:10 Nina (Cloud Infra): that works.
00:33:15 Oliver (CISO): risk thing — if we provide a temporary outbound channel for PS to patch, what's the least-priv model?
00:33:23 Evan (SE): we can request a short-lived peering tunnel or a signed maintenance bundle; PS will authenticate via mutual TLS and ops tokens and actions are audited.
00:33:36 Jade (Compliance): good.
00:33:40 Dana (AE): wrapping up — let's recap next steps, assign owners.
00:33:46 Dana (AE): Evan to provide KMS integration doc and example KMIP flows (action).
00:33:49 Evan (SE): action noted.
00:33:51 Dana (AE): I'll send SOC2 evidence starter pack.
00:33:54 Dana (AE): Nina to send network diagrams and proxy configs.
00:33:56 Nina (Cloud Infra): will do.
00:33:58 Dana (AE): we'll schedule a hands-on workshop week of 12/29.
00:34:02 Priya (Redwood): noted.
00:34:05 Oliver (CISO): any final open questions?
00:34:08 Samir (Security Architect): only request — please include an example key rotation timeline for auditors.
00:34:13 Evan (SE): will include with KMS doc.
00:34:18 Dana (AE): great. thanks everyone. we'll follow up by EOW with the artifacts.
